{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZi_Q-A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDJud0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 69, "title": "Correct V30MZ external IRQ entry timing in both delivery paths", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `793eb58c688821ef6a601cad2472a07ebc19bc83`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:371,388` charges external IRQ entry as 12 execution clocks plus entry transfers. Aligned internal vector/stack accesses therefore total 17 clocks; odd internal stacks total 20. `cpu/word_transfer_tests.rs` explicitly expects those totals.

This undercounts ordinary VBlank, raster and timer interrupt handling, changing its relationship to video, timers, audio and DMA. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

Correct external IRQ entry accounting before instruction execution and when external IRQ wins arbitration at an eligible single-step boundary. Preserve architectural delivery behavior and existing transfer penalties across emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations.

Keep this task focused on external IRQ entry and necessary cross-file validation. Full prefetch, instruction-wide timing corrections, new interrupt sources and external bus-policy changes remain separate work.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 68 closed titles were checked without finding an equivalent completed correction.

The [NEC V30MZ manual](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), Table 5-1 and its note, specifies 32 clocks from interruption to handler entry, excluding inserted waits and holds. Chapter 4 establishes alignment penalties and two aligned vector reads. This is core documentation; exact console phases remain unmeasured. Extracted text was inspected; PDF screenshot retrieval failed.

Accounting inference for the existing serialized emulator: the five baseline vector/stack transfers already belong within 32. Therefore use `27 + actual entry-transfer charges`, preserving extra split-transfer/wait costs. A preceding instruction retains its own cost. [Pinned ares dispatch](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/blob/c76aaffa6e69778baf9a66d1da04298ac2ed7d1d/ares/component/processor/v30mz/instruction.cpp) also distinguishes external INT timing, but its scheduler differs and its constants must not be transplanted directly.

Correction record: old AI-authored assumption—17/20 clocks are suitable complete external IRQ entry totals. Corrected requirement—32 clocks for aligned internal entry, with additional transfer penalties counted once. The manual contradicts the old totals. Preserve [Issue #39](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/39)'s raw transfer acceptance and [Issue #67](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/67)'s delivery semantics; both left this absolute timing correction separate. Record further evidence-backed corrections with the old assumption, replacement requirement, source and rationale, without a human-approval gate.

Existing tests cover transfer costs, IRQ/trap arbitration, REP/HALT, DMA precedence and shared scheduling. [Saved #67 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/793eb58c688821ef6a601cad2472a07ebc19bc83/docs/issue-67-validation.md) reports 227 workspace tests and complete production Chromium suites passing. These are reported execution results; this planning inspection ran no builds or tests.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the entry accounting and independent expected vectors before changing timing. Distinguish entry, preceding instruction, handler instructions and DMA stalls. Preserve existing bus classification and explicitly retain unresolved Mono external-wait behavior.
- [ ] Correct both external IRQ delivery paths without double-counting baseline transfers or the preceding instruction. Add literal native expectations: aligned internal entry 32 clocks, odd internal stack 35; RAM NOP followed by boundary-selected IRQ 34/37 respectively. These checks must fail against the baseline.
- [ ] Cover Color/Crystal SRAM stacks with existing waits clear/set: entry totals 35/41 clocks, derived from two internal vector reads and six byte writes. Cover aligned/odd stacks and selected segment-offset/20-bit boundary cases using independently calculated literal costs and frame bytes, never production accounting helpers as the oracle.
- [ ] Exercise all nine supported model/mode combinations and runtime mode transitions. Preserve vector priority, normalized saved IP/CS/FLAGS, stack order/SP, live IF/TF clearing, acknowledgement and IRET continuation. Retain IRQ-shadow, simultaneous IRQ/TF, synchronous-entry, REP restart/progress, HALT wake/idle and DMA-before-IRQ regression coverage. Keep single-step-only entry costs unchanged.
- [ ] Add normal `Machine::run_frame` checks proving corrected IRQ costs advance raster/frame state, timers and audio exactly once, without executing an extra application instruction. Preserve separate GDMA/SDMA stall accounting and capability gates.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 timing cartridge and independent native/production-browser consumers. Measure an absolute IRQ-heavy execution budget, for example a bounded repeated-latched-IRQ sequence, including separately derived harness costs and timer quantization. An aligned-versus-odd delta alone is insufficient because the old baseline preserves that delta. Record an actual baseline failure and corrected native and production Chromium passes, with CPU-written timing/count/continuation observations on every model, supported runtime modes and fresh restart. Poison or invalidate stale completion data so retained saves cannot fabricate success.
- [ ] Preserve firmware-free startup, three-model behavior, LCD/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/cartridge/internal EEPROM and RTC retention, browser save integrity, browser-local data handling and ownership/provenance. Coordinator runs and records `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview, including the IRQ probe.
- [ ] Update hardware timing documentation, fixture provenance and validation evidence, including tested source/artifact identities, failures, corrections and unperformed checks. Coordinator reviews the final diff and actual results against every criterion and resolves blocking findings before merge. Preserve relevant prior acceptance when correcting technical assumptions.

## Optional validation

Additional lawful software timing experiments, browser engines or console comparisons may supply further evidence. These and human gameplay were unperformed during planning. Proprietary ROMs or firmware are unnecessary for mandatory acceptance.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
